# Intake: Audit-runner pi calls crash with `Connection error.` from stale-ctx extension exceptions

## Problem statement

Audit-runner `pi` subprocesses crash mid-call and the runner records
`provider_error: Connection error.` because pi extensions loaded into the audit
session throw on a **stale `ExtensionContext`** after pi replaces or reloads the
session. The **fatal uncaught exception** is thrown by the ContextHub-owned
`worklog` recovery extension (`register-recovery.ts`, `_notifyFn` →
`ctx.ui.notify`), not by `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge`. Two
SorraAgents-owned extensions (`proxy-compaction-bridge` and `proxy-sse-signals`)
throw the *same* stale-ctx error but pi catches those and prints them as
(non-fatal) `Extension error (...)` lines. This blocks audits and therefore the
ship final-validation gate (exit 12).

## Users

- **Release manager** — needs audits to complete so `dev` → `main` is not blocked
  by spurious provider failures.
  - *As a release manager, I want an audit pi call to return a genuine verdict
    even after an extension-triggered session replacement, so the release gate
    is not blocked by an infrastructure crash.*
- **Audit operator** — needs `provider_error` entries in the debug corpus to
  reflect real provider faults, not extension crashes.
  - *As an audit operator, I want the audit debug log to distinguish a real
    provider fault from an extension exception, so I can triage correctly.*
- **Pi extension maintainer** — needs extensions to fail safe when the session
  they were registered against is replaced.
  - *As a maintainer, I want my extension's async callbacks to no-op when the
    captured ctx is invalid, so a session swap cannot crash an unrelated run.*

## Existing state (evidence)

The failure was captured for the audit of **SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB** (now deleted).
The debug log `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB.jsonl`
(`context=parent`) records:

- `reason: provider_error`, `provider_error: "Connection error."`,
  `elapsed_seconds: ~713`.
- `raw_stderr` contains one `Extension error
  (/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts): This
  extension ctx is stale ...` line, one identical line for
  `proxy-sse-signals`, and then the **fatal, uncaught** trace:

  ```
  Error: This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload. ...
      at ExtensionRunner.assertActive (...)
      at get ui (...)
      at _notifyFn (/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts:71:41)
      at _notifyRetryAttempt (.../register-recovery.ts:549:5)
      at triggerInvisibleContinue (.../register-recovery.ts:391:7)
      at process.processTicksAndRejections (...)
  Node.js v22.22.1
  ```

  The trailing `Node.js v22.22.1` banner shows the pi process **crashed**; the
  audit runner then surfaced `Connection error.` from the pi JSON stream.

Corpus scan across every `reason=provider_error` entry
(`~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl`) shows **all** non-empty
`raw_stderr` provider errors carry the `register-recovery.ts` stale-ctx stack;
some also carry the `proxy-compaction-bridge` / `proxy-sse-signals`
`Extension error` lines (non-fatal, caught by pi).

Root cause of each stale access:

- `ContextHub .../register-recovery.ts` — `_notifyFn` is assigned a closure over
  the *handler's* `ctx` (`_notifyFn = (message, level) => ctx.ui.notify(...)`,
  lines ~84/87/212) and is later invoked from the async retry loop
  (`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`). If the session was replaced/reloaded in
  between, `ctx.ui` throws — and because the call originates in a timer/async
  callback, pi never catches it and the process dies.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts` — both `after_provider_response`
  and `context` handlers call `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()` on the event
  ctx; a stale ctx throws.
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts` — `turn_start` captures `ctx.ui` as
  `statusUi`; the capturing-fetch callback later calls `statusUi.setStatus(...)`
  on the stale UI handle.

`pi` supports `--no-extensions` / `-ne` (disables extension discovery), alongside
the `--no-context-files --no-skills` flags the audit runner already adds to
`_call_pi`. Audit prompts are read-only and fully self-contained, so they do not
depend on extensions.

## Desired change

1. **Unblock audit calls (SorraAgents-owned):** stop loading interactive/UI
   extensions in audit-runner pi subprocesses — add `--no-extensions` to the
   `_call_pi` command (mirroring the existing context-reduction flags).
2. **Harden the SorraAgents-owned extensions:** make `proxy-compaction-bridge`
   and `proxy-sse-signals` fail safe on a stale/replaced ctx — never call
   `ctx.ui`/`ctx.sessionManager` on an invalidated ctx (guard, re-capture from a
   fresh handler, or no-op/passthrough).
3. **Fatal crash (cross-repo handoff — delivered):** the ContextHub
   `worklog` recovery-extension stale-ctx crash is handed off to
   **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** (`Worklog recovery extension crashes pi on stale
   ExtensionContext after session replacement (_notifyFn)`), which is not edited
   from this SorraAgents work item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **No extension crash on audit calls:** the audit runner's `_call_pi` command
   excludes extension discovery (`--no-extensions`). Verified by a unit test
   asserting the constructed command (both tool-enabled and tool-disabled paths).
2. **Stale-ctx-safe SorraAgents extensions:** `proxy-compaction-bridge` and
   `proxy-sse-signals` no-op (context passthrough / status unchanged) when their
   handler or async callback observes an invalidated `ctx`, never throwing.
   Verified by `node:test` unit tests injecting a stale-ctx stub.
3. **Re-audit completes genuinely:** a re-audit of SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB (or an
   equivalent audit pi call that triggers a session replacement) completes with a
   genuine verdict (`met`/`partial`/`adjusted`) and the debug entry's `reason` is
   not `provider_error` with `Connection error.` attributable to an extension
   exception.
4. **Regression tests:** a stale/replaced-session-ctx regression test exists for
   both `pi-client` extensions (Node unit tests) and a Python test asserts the
   audit `_call_pi` command includes `--no-extensions`; the tests fail against
   the pre-fix code.
5. **Docs + full suite:** `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` and
   `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md` (F6) are updated to reflect the corrected
   attribution/fix; all related documentation (code comments, README, docs) is
   updated; and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo boundary:** the fatal crash is in
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub` (separate repo and `WL-` worklog). It is
  **not** edited from this item; the fix is tracked in WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B.
- **Do not regress** the compaction-bridge wire contract
  (LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8) or the dispatch reshape semantics/tests.
- **Do not weaken fail-closed audit behaviour**; the audit runner must still
  return `unmet`/`partial` on genuine provider errors, not mask them.
- `--no-extensions` affects all discovered extensions in audit calls only; the
  interactive TUI extension behaviour (compaction mirroring, status line,
  recovery) must remain unchanged.
- `wl`-tracked, test-first, build → test → commit.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi` builds the pi command
  (~L3648); add `--no-extensions`.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — command-flag tests (~L267–304);
  add the `--no-extensions` assertion.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts` — guard/re-bind the session id
  used by `after_provider_response` and `context` handlers.
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js` — pure core (no ctx
  access); keep behaviour, extend tests only.
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts` — guard the captured `statusUi` used by
  the capturing-fetch callback.
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`,
  `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs` — stale-ctx regression coverage.
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md`, `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md` —
  documentation/correction.
- *(cross-repo, tracked in WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B)*
  `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts`.

## Related work (manual)

- **SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB** — `[test-failure] getCompletedOrInReviewItems ...`
  (`discovered-from`; the audit that failed with this signature; now deleted).
- **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** — Ship skill: parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules for
  child audits in the final-validation gate (records the same failure as the
  motivation for removing manual interruptions).
- **SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL** — RCA: Audit Pipeline Reliability
  (`docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md`); F6 documents the 9 `provider_error`
  entries (incl. `Connection error.`) and their conflation with parse failures.
- **SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0** — origin of `proxy-compaction-bridge` (wire contract
  LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8).
- **SA-0MSHAKSEA001LQ6T** — origin of `proxy-sse-signals`.
- **SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U** — audit context reduction
  (`--no-context-files --no-skills`); precedent for adding a loader flag to
  `_call_pi`.
- **WL-0MUIV50EJ007VH9B** (ContextHub) — handoff item for the fatal
  `register-recovery.ts` stale-ctx crash.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope/cross-repo).** Debug-log evidence shows the *fatal* uncaught
  exception is thrown by the ContextHub-owned `worklog` extension
  (`register-recovery.ts`), not `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge`. How should
  this item be scoped?
  - Answer (producer): **(c) analysis/handoff** — do not edit ContextHub from this

## Problem statement

Discovered during the find-related v3 review (discovered-from:SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9).

A full-suite run can enter unbounded recursion when the test cache is cold (e.g. a fresh worktree/commit) and/or another full-suite run is executing concurrently. The audit child-cascade test spawns a **real** `audit_runner.py issue` subprocess, which auto-executes the full test suite (full-suite cache miss), which re-runs the same test, which spawns another real child audit, and so on.

## Evidence

Observed recursion (process tree), during `/skill:test` / `implement.py finish` in a worktree:

```
run_tests.py --scope full
└── pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings
    └── (test) skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py
        ::TestChildPersistFailureFatal::test_child_persist_not_found_aborts_run
        └── audit_runner.py issue OSL-2 --pi-bin pi --model Local Proxy/plan \
              --model-source local --force \
              --worklog-dir /tmp/pytest-of-*/pytest-NNN/test_child_persist_not_found_a0/...
            └── python3 -m pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings   # nested full suite
                └── ... (repeats; observed 19-50+ nested processes)
```

- My `implement.py finish` timed out after 1500s; a plain `run_tests.py --scope full` also timed out (>1500s).
- The offending test passes in isolation (`TestChildPersistFailureFatal` — 2 passed in 1.44s) and the full suite passes sequentially on a warm cache (`success: True`, 350s, 2743 passed).
- Trigger conditions observed: cold test cache (fresh worktree/commit) combined with concurrent full-suite execution.

## Root cause (hypothesis)

`TestChildPersistFailureFatal._run_with_child()` calls `audit_runner.cmd_issue(..., audit_children=True)` with a **faked wl runner**, but the `audit_children` path issues a real `subprocess.run(audit_cmd, ...)` for the child audit (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~line 9594). The real child audit resolves `full_suite_commands()` against the process cwd (the repository) and, on a full-suite cache miss, auto-executes the real suite — including this test. Nothing caps the nesting, so a cold cache recurses until the outer timeout.

## Proposed fix

- Mock the child-audit subprocess in `TestChildPersistFailureFatal` (as other audit tests do with a mock `--pi-bin`), so no real child audit runs.
- Add a recursion guard so an auto-triggered child suite run cannot itself auto-trigger another (e.g. an env marker / `--no-auto-green-run` propagated to children spawned under test).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `run_tests.py --scope full` completes (no recursion) from a cold test cache in a fresh worktree
- [ ] A regression test proves a child-audit cascade cannot re-enter the full suite (bounded, fails fast)
- [ ] `TestChildPersistFailureFatal` still asserts its intended behaviour (non-zero rc + "Aborting" error on persist failure)
- [ ] Full suite remains green sequentially

## Constraints

- Do not weaken real child-audit behaviour in production; the guard applies to test/auto-run contexts.

# implement.py finish leaves local dev behind after pushing to remote dev

Counterpart of the AI_Hell discovery report **AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB**
(`discovered-from:AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB`). The defect is in agent infrastructure in this
repository — `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`. The full discovery context (observed
commits, parent run, workaround) is on the AI_Hell report; this item is the actionable fix.

## Headline

After `implement.py finish <child>` pushes the child's branch to `origin/dev`, the main
checkout's local `dev` branch is left one or more commits behind, so the next
`implement.py parent <epic>` / `implement.py start <child>` creates the following child's
worktree from a stale base and is missing the previous sibling's files.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` restores the main checkout to the parent branch **before** pushing the
just-committed branch to `origin dev`:

- Step 7 — `_restore_repo_state(repo_root)` runs `git checkout dev` then `git pull origin dev`
  (local `dev` fast-forwards only to the **pre-push** remote tip).
- Step 8 — `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch)` runs
  `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` (the new commit lands on the remote after the pull).

Local `dev` is therefore left behind. `git_worktree_add()` forks each child from the **local**
parent branch (`git worktree add --track -b <branch> <worktree> dev`) and `phase_start`
performs no fetch, so every subsequent child starts from the stale base.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running the parent/epic flow (`implement.py parent`).
- **Operators / orchestrators** relying on the parent flow being self-consistent without
  manual `git fetch` / `git merge` steps.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, after `finish` reports "commit pushed to dev", I want the main
  checkout's local `dev` to contain that commit, so the next `parent`/`start` child worktree
  includes my just-finished sibling's files.
- As an operator, I want the parent flow to never create a child from a stale base, so I do
  not have to diagnose phantom build errors or risk lost/duplicated work.

## Observed (from AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB)

- F2 (`AH-0MUBYU600004YU4T`) `finish` pushed `91538d0` to `origin/dev`; local `dev` stayed at
  `1920e65`.
- The F3 worktree (`AH-0MUBYXR280018HST`) was created from local `dev` `1920e65` and could not
  resolve `../powerups/collectAnimation` (added by F2) until local `dev` was manually
  fast-forwarded and merged into the worktree.
- Workaround applied by hand during the parent `AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W` run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Post-push local parent sync.** After a successful push in `phase_finish`, the
  main checkout's local parent branch (`dev`) is at least as advanced as the pushed tip when
  it is safe to fast-forward (local `dev` == pushed commit == `origin/dev`).
- [ ] **AC2 — Safe-skip semantics.** When the update is not safe (dirty main checkout, other
  branch/detached, or local `dev` diverged), `finish` does not force it, loses no local
  commits, and does not fail. The skip is reported and the repo remains recoverable.
- [ ] **AC3 — Children never start from a stale base.** `parent`/`start` refresh the parent
  branch (`fetch` + fast-forward) before `git worktree add`, or fork from
  `origin/<parent_branch>` after a fetch.
- [ ] **AC4 — Regression tests.** A focused regression test (e.g.
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`) covers AC1–AC3; existing
  `tests/test_implement_*.py` still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated** (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`, code comments, README and
  any relevant docs-site entries) for the new post-push sync and safe-skip semantics.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies; reuse stdlib and the existing `run_cmd` / `git_*` helpers.
- Never force-update a branch with local commits; prefer `--ff-only`.
- Must not regress worktree-based finish (worktree is removed before the push).
- Remote-unreachable / dirty-checkout paths degrade gracefully (report, do not fail a finish
  that already pushed successfully).
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_PARENT_BRANCH = "dev"`.
- `_restore_repo_state(repo_root)` → `git checkout dev`; `git pull origin dev`.
- `git_push_to_dev(cwd, branch)` → `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev`.
- `git_worktree_add(branch, worktree_path, parent_branch)` → `git worktree add --track -b ...`;
  `phase_start` does no fetch.
- `phase_finish` order: remove worktree → `_restore_repo_state` → `git_push_to_dev`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — reorder/guard the post-push local parent sync and
  refresh the parent branch in `phase_start` before `git_worktree_add`.
- `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` — new regression test for AC1–AC3.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` —
  extend parent-flow coverage (fresh base for the next child).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the post-push local parent sync and safe-skip semantics.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB** — AI_Hell discovery report (this item's origin).
- **AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W** — AI_Hell parent epic where the stale base was observed.
- **SA-0MT9607Q5009JA2V** — precedent AI_Hell→SorraAgents counterpart pattern.
- **SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM** — prior worktree-awareness work in the implement flow.
- **SA-0MSIVM00X003E5PZ**, **SA-0MSI8YLTN0007KN8** — other `phase_finish` robustness fixes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** auto-updating local `dev` could clobber intentional local commits — mitigate with a
  clean/on-branch/no-divergence guard and `--ff-only`.
- **Risk:** `git pull`/`fetch` in a dirty or offline main checkout — never fail a finish that
  already pushed.
- **Risk (scope creep):** a generic "sync all worktrees" mechanism or changing the
  push-to-`dev` policy are out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which repository owns the fix?** — **Answer (agent research):** SorraAgents (this repo).
  Evidence: `implement.py` lives here and the global skill is a symlink into this repo; AI_Hell
  contains no `implement.py`.
- **Q: Is the bug still present?** — **Answer (agent research):** yes, `_restore_repo_state`
  runs before `git_push_to_dev` in `phase_finish`.

`implement.py finish` runs the test suite via `skill/test_cache.run_cached` with a direct `pytest` command, so it does NOT set `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE=1`. `implement.py run_tests` should set `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE=1` in the subprocess environment when invoking the inner pytest (mirroring `run_tests.py`), so the outer/inner guard ownership is consistent and finish does not crash on subprocess-patching tests. ## Problem

`implement.py finish` pushes with a hard-coded 120 s timeout:

```
ERROR: Unhandled exception: Command '['git', 'push', ...]' timed out after 120 seconds
```

But the repo's `.githooks/pre-push` runs the **full test suite** for pushes
targeting `refs/heads/dev|main` (`run_tests.py --scope full`). Any project whose
full suite takes longer than 120 s therefore cannot complete `implement.py
finish`: the commit succeeds, but the push is killed, the worktree is removed,
and the item is left `open` (safety reset) with the commit stranded on the
feature branch. Observed for both the companion cleanup (commit e36dd153) and
the F7 verification (commit 649ff913), each requiring a manual background push.

Worse, killing the `git push` does not kill the pre-push hook's child
`run_tests.py`: orphaned hook processes survived and deadlocked a subsequent
push attempt (both waiting on the same cache lock). Manual `kill` of the
orphaned hooks was required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** The `finish` push timeout is configurable and defaults to a value that
  accommodates the repo's pre-push gate (e.g. reuse `timeoutPerCommand` from
  `.pi/test-config.json`, currently 1500 s) rather than a fixed 120 s.
  *Verification:* a test proves a slow pre-push hook no longer times out.
- **AC2** On push timeout, `finish` terminates the spawned hook children (process
  group kill), leaving no orphaned `run_tests.py`/hook processes.
  *Verification:* a test simulating a slow hook asserts no surviving child.
- **AC3** A push timeout leaves recoverable state: the commit hash and the
  feature branch are reported, and the work item is not silently reset without
  an actionable message.
  *Verification:* a test asserts the finish report names the commit hash and
  branch and that a manual-push comment is posted on timeout.
- **AC4** Full suite passes; docs (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`,
  `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`) describe the timeout behaviour.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` push call, its hard-coded
  `timeout=120` in `git_push_to_dev()`, and the existing `_resolve_test_timeout()`
  helper (reads `.pi/test-config.json`) to reuse for the configurable timeout.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `timeoutPerCommand` config reader (reuse).
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — new tests for AC1/AC2/AC3 (slow-hook
  timeout, process-group kill, recoverable-state reporting).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the timeout contract.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — implementation-reference detail for
  the timeout behaviour.

## Plan

Single-item bug fix (effort XS / risk Low) — no child work items required.
Implementation order: (1) make the push timeout configurable via the existing
`_resolve_test_timeout()` reader; (2) spawn the push in its own process group
and kill the group on timeout; (3) surface commit hash + branch + manual-push
comment on timeout; (4) add tests then docs. Test-first per AC verification.

# live-repo mutation guard false-positives when the suite runs inside an agent worktree

`discovered-from:SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`

## Problem statement

When the full test suite runs **inside an agent worktree** (the normal `implement.py finish` and `/skill:test` case), the live-repo mutation guard anchors its agent-worktree exclusion on the *passed root* rather than the **main checkout**. Inside a linked worktree that root is the worktree itself, so `excluded_refs` is always empty and any concurrent agent committing to another worktree is reported as a mutation — failing the run and blocking the full-suite release gate for every agent whenever the shared host has more than one active session.

## Users

- **Primary:** AI agents running `/skill:test` or `implement.py finish` from inside an `implement` worktree on a shared multi-agent host.
- **Secondary:** the human producer relying on the full-suite exit code as the pre-push release gate.
- **Tertiary:** maintainers of the shared `git_sandbox.py` helper and the two guards that consume it.

Example user stories:

- As an **implementing agent**, I want the full suite to run green inside my worktree even while sibling agents commit to theirs, so that concurrent sessions do not block my release gate.
- As a **producer**, I want the guard to keep failing on genuine in-place mutation of the guarded checkout, so that real corruption (the `GIT_DIR` incident, SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX) is never reported as green.
- As a **maintainer**, I want one shared fix in `git_sandbox.py`, so the outer `run_tests.py` guard and the inner `live_repo_guard.py` conftest guard cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `snapshot_repo_state()` called with a **linked-worktree root** returns `excluded_refs` containing every branch checked out in a registered worktree under the **main checkout's** `.worklog/worktrees/` (not `<passed_root>/.worklog/worktrees`). Verification: a unit test creates a main repo plus an agent worktree, calls `snapshot_repo_state(worktree_root)`, and asserts the agent worktree's `refs/heads/wl-*` is in `excluded_refs`.
- [ ] **No false positive:** with the guard/snapshot armed at a linked-worktree root, advancing a branch checked out in a *sibling* agent worktree produces `diff_snapshots(before, after)["changed"] == False` and does not fail the guard. Verification: a nested-pytest test that arms the guard inside a worktree, commits in a sibling worktree, and asserts exit code 0 with no `live-repo mutation` text (red on the pre-fix helper).
- [ ] **No false negative:** an in-place mutation of the guarded checkout is still reported — (a) moving `HEAD`/the guarded branch ref, (b) modifying a tracked file, (c) adding an untracked non-ignored file. Verification: the existing `TestSnapshotContract` cases still pass when the guard is armed at a worktree root.
- [ ] **Worktree registration churn does not fail:** registering or removing a worktree under `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` during a guarded run does not fail the guard when the reportable diff is empty. Verification: a unit test where `excluded_refs` grows but `diff_snapshots` reports `changed == False` asserts the per-test guard does not fail.
- [ ] **Single shared fix:** both the `run_tests.py` outer guard (`_detect_live_repo_mutation`) and the conftest inner guard (`live_repo_guard.py`) exhibit the corrected behaviour, with the anchoring logic living only in `git_sandbox.py`. Verification: code review plus the guard-level nested-pytest tests.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the reported failure (red against the pre-fix helper) and passes after the fix, covering the `wl-SA-0MUD5R5EQ...-fix-inherited-pass...` worktree scenario and the observed `moved ref refs/heads/wl-*` suite failures.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. This includes the `git_sandbox.py` module docstring's exclusion-derivation note and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` must remain **stdlib-only** and loadable by file location — the repo-root `conftest.py` loads it via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` and must not mutate `sys.path`.
- Agent-worktree exclusion must be **derived from git plumbing** (e.g. `git worktree list --porcelain`, or `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` to locate the main checkout) — **never** a `wl-*` name pattern. The module docstring documents why: a name pattern would also exclude the incident's own fixture branches and destroy detection of the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX class of bug.
- Snapshots stay **read-only**: only plumbing commands; never `gc`, `update-index`, `fetch`, or `--refresh`.
- The fix must not weaken genuine mutation detection (moved `dev`, config rewrites, tracked/untracked file changes).
- Any extra git invocation per snapshot must be cheap and confined to the snapshot path; it must not turn the per-test fingerprint into a full `status` scan.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::_parse_worktrees` computes `agent_root = root.joinpath(*AGENT_WORKTREE_DIR)`, where `root` is the passed root (for `snapshot_repo_state`, the `git_toplevel(resolved)` of the passed path).
- Reproduced 2026-09-26 on `dev @ 10995367`:
  - `snapshot_repo_state(".")` from the **main checkout** → `excluded_refs` contains all 12 agent-worktree branches.
  - `snapshot_repo_state(".")` from `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSRN0Q64005YR5A-stale-pytest-exit` → `git_toplevel` is the worktree root and `excluded_refs == set()`.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` arms with `root` from `_default_root(config)` (or the repo-root conftest's `_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent`, which inside a worktree is the worktree root).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_detect_live_repo_mutation` calls `snapshot_repo_state(project_root)` where `project_root` comes from `detect_project_root()` (worktree root when run inside one). It shares the same helper and the same defect.
- Adjacent defect (same guard path, reproduced): `fingerprint()` includes `tuple(sorted(excluded))`, and `pytest_runtest_teardown` fails whenever the fingerprint differs — regardless of `diff_snapshots(...)["changed"]`. Adding a second worktree under `.worklog/worktrees/` mid-run changes `excluded` while the diff stays clean, so worktree registration churn is a second false positive.
- Existing tests only arm the guard at the **main** root (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestLiveRepoGuard::test_agent_worktree_churn_does_not_trip_the_guard` creates the worktree under the root it arms), so they do not exercise the linked-worktree case.

Minimal reproduction (from any linked worktree):


# audit_runner failure-restore reuses an invalid pre-audit status/stage combo, leaving items unrecoverable

## Problem statement

When an audit ends in an infrastructure-failure / fallback-tainted "Ready to close: No" verdict, `audit_runner.py` restores the captured pre-audit `status`+`stage` verbatim. If that captured combination is already invalid (which happens when an item was imported/refiled with status and stage set independently), every restore attempt is rejected by `wl` and the item is left in an unresolved, inconsistent state.

Observed during the audit of SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD on 2026-09-26 (session herdr-1790437388-2668941-15858, log `/home/rgardler/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD-20260926-173301.log`):

- Phase 1 parent screening hit audit-concurrency starvation (no slot within 90s) → unparseable → infra-fallback `partial` for all ACs.
- `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` correctly chose the restore branch (infra-fallback "No"), building `wl update <id> --status <captured> --stage <captured> --assignee ""`.
- The captured combo was invalid, so all 3 attempts failed:
  `Invalid status/stage combination: status "blocked" is not compatible with stage "in_review"`.
- The runner then printed "the item's lifecycle is unresolved — recover manually" and exited non-zero; `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` failed identically.

(A prior, separate observation during the same run: the item's pre-audit status was already invalid for its stage — `wl` allows stage `in_review` only with status `completed`, yet the item sat at `in-progress`/`in_review`.)

## Root cause

`_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (~L10672) and `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` (~L10624) only substitute a safe stage when `safe_stage` is falsy. A present-but-invalid captured combo is used as-is, so the restore cannot succeed and the item is stranded in an invalid combination.

## Desired change

Before applying a restore (or a "No" demotion), validate the intended `(status, stage)` pair against `wl`'s allowed combinations and coerce to the nearest valid pair (e.g. keep the status but fall back to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete` for the stage), or retry with a stage-agnostic update. Never leave an item in an invalid combination after the runner exits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the captured pre-audit `(status, stage)` combination is invalid, the failure/restore path applies a valid, consistent state instead of failing all attempts, and the runner never leaves the item in an invalid combination.
2. A regression test covers restoring an item whose captured combo is invalid (e.g. `blocked`/`in_review`) and asserts a valid terminal state is reached.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_apply_terminal_lifecycle`, `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` — lifecycle/restore regression tests

## Evidence

- Audit log: `/home/rgardler/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD-20260926-173301.log`
- Persisted report: `wl audit-show SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD --json`
- Recorded under producer answer Q4 (comment SA-C0MUIO0LQY005GG74 on SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD)

## Summary

The 2026-09-26 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident (SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX) was rooted in a repository-override git environment variable exported into agent/test sessions by a launcher **outside** the `skill/` tree. Defence-in-depth now neutralises the *effect* at every in-repo execution path, but the launcher can still export a live-repo `GIT_DIR` (plus `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`) into the **pre-scrub** environment of any process that calls `git` directly. This item investigates that export and removes or scopes it at its source.

## Problem statement

On 2026-09-26 an orphaned audit fan-out inherited `GIT_DIR=<live worktree git dir>`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` and `GIT_PREFIX=` from a launcher outside the `skill/` tree. The in-repo defence-in-depth layers (shared env scrub, release-gate fail-fast, host-wide audit cap) stop that value from reaching test subprocesses, but they remain the only protection: anything spawned before the scrub that calls `git` itself can still be redirected into the live checkout. The exporting process has not been identified and no setter exists inside this repository.

## Users

- **Agent operators / maintainers** running autonomous agents through herdr/Pi: need every freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables.
- **Contributors** sharing the live checkout: need `dev`/`origin/dev` protected even when a launcher is misconfigured.

User stories:

- As an operator, I want a freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables, so a misconfigured launcher can never redirect a git command into the live checkout.
- As a maintainer, I want the process that sets the override identified and fixed at source, so the defence-in-depth scrub is not the only line of protection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exporting process/script is identified with reproducible, non-destructive evidence (environment of a freshly spawned agent session or a traced process ancestry), and the evidence is recorded in the work item.
- [ ] The export is removed or scoped at source so child processes — panes, `audit_runner`, `run_tests`, and direct `git` calls — never inherit a live-repo `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`.
- [ ] A regression check asserts a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables before any git-touching step; it fails if such a variable is reintroduced.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 (residual launcher risk) is updated to name the confirmed source and the fix, or to record why the source could not be confirmed.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Non-destructive investigation.** The live checkout must never be mutated; evidence gathering must use throwaway/fixture repositories and must never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Source, not symptom.** The fix must be at the exporting launcher, not merely another in-repo scrub layer.
- **Cross-repo.** The likely launcher lives in the ContextHub repository (`packages/herdr`), outside this worklog's repo — see Open Question 1.

## Existing state

Defence-in-depth landed under SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX:

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` + `scrub_repository_overrides` / `repository_override_vars_present` / `log_repository_override_scrub`.
- `skill/test_cache.py::_default_runner`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_run_cmd`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi` pass scrubbed `env=`.
- `run_tests.py --strict-git-env` release-gate fail-fast (invoked by `.githooks/pre-push` for `dev`/`main`).
- `audit_runner.main` host-wide audit cap + `_find_orphaned_audit_processes` / `_warn_on_orphaned_audits`.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 documents the residual external-launcher risk.

Confirmed by search (`rg 'export GIT_|GIT_DIR='` across the repo and tooling): **no setter exists in the SorraAgents repository**. Candidate launchers identified:

- **herdr agent launcher** (ContextHub, external): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` → `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, invoked as `herdr pane run <pane> exec bash run-pi-agent.sh <lease> ...`.
- **herdr downtime worker** (external): `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` forwards `...process.env` to `send-to-pi.sh`, adding only `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` and `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`. It does **not** scrub repository-override vars, so a `GIT_DIR` already present in the herdr process propagates to every spawned pane.
- **git-hook chain** (in repo): `.git/hooks/post-checkout|post-merge|post-rewrite` delegate to `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` → `wl sync`. Git sets `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH` and `GIT_PREFIX` when running hooks, and `implement.py`'s `git_worktree_add` (`git worktree add`) triggers `post-checkout`. The observed `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` + empty `GIT_PREFIX` are the exact git-hook signature, so the poisoned environment was most plausibly inherited from a git-spawned child rather than a static shell `export`.

## Desired change

1. Determine the **origin** of `GIT_DIR` in the launcher environment — which process first set it and why — using non-destructive evidence: `/proc/<pid>/environ` of pane/agent/audit processes, git `trace2` (`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`) around `git worktree add`/hooks, and launcher/hook inspection.
2. Fix at source: scrub (or refuse to propagate) `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` in the launcher spawn path (e.g. herdr `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`, `run-pi-agent.sh`/`send-to-pi.sh`) and/or stop the git-hook child that leaks the variables.
3. Add a regression check that a fresh agent/test session has no repository-override variables.
4. Update §9.3 with the finding and fix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — update §9.3 with the confirmed source and fix.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — shared override-var list/scrub helper (reuse for any in-repo mitigation or regression check).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — fresh-session regression check and `--strict-git-env` integration.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — orphan/env-evidence hooks for reproducing the audit fan-out condition safely.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add` flow that triggers the `post-checkout` hook.
- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite`, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — hook chain (`wl sync`) executed by git with `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` set.
- External (ContextHub, cross-repo — see Open Question 1): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX** – Test/audit runner leaks GIT_DIR into test subprocesses, corrupting the live checkout and origin/dev (parent incident; completed/in_review).
- Children of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX: SA-0MUIULHQC005MUM0 (shared scrub helper), SA-0MUIUMK9Y008SCE0 (scrub in execution paths), SA-0MUIULX49001BWGG (release-gate fail-fast), SA-0MUIULC2Y009XYM1 (regression tests), SA-0MUIUMBL8002HBYH (docs + full suite), SA-0MUIUMO7T00639FL (host-wide audit cap + orphan detection).
- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX** – Restore wl sync: main-checkout git identity was left as incident-era `T <t@t.com>` (residual incident recovery).
- **SA-0MUIBWORE001HOLK** – Symlink nested node_modules into implement worktrees (the worktree whose git dir appeared in the leaked `GIT_DIR`).

### Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MS0DK6BD001RNDG** – implement.py abort script deletes entire project directory when aborting from main working tree (completed)
- **SA-0MSAXHMZT009EHVV** – cwd-independent wl invocation and real diagnostics (completed)
- **SA-0MPDZDVG00013CQJ** – Implement: Agent push-to-dev behavior (completed)

Repository file matches: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the incident evidence (process env at the time) is gone; reproduction could itself endanger the live checkout. **Mitigation:** use a throwaway repo + `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`; never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Risk:** fixing only the identified launcher leaves other propagation paths. **Mitigation:** scrub at the launcher spawn boundary (one choke point) plus the regression check.
- **Risk (scope creep):** hardening every launcher is broader than this investigation. **Mitigation:** record additional opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this item.
- **Assumption:** the leak is architectural (environment propagation through the launcher) rather than a one-off manual `export`.
- **Assumption:** the `GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` signature indicates a git-spawned child origin; if tracing shows otherwise, the evidence will redirect the fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope / repo):** The candidate launchers are external to SorraAgents (ContextHub `packages/herdr`) and the git-hook chain that runs `wl sync`. Where should the fix land? Options: (A) investigate + evidence in SorraAgents (this item); if herdr is the culprit, file a cross-repo ContextHub work item and link it; (B) fix entirely within SorraAgents by hardening the git hooks / adding a wrapper; (C) transfer this item to ContextHub. **Recommended:** A — keeps the incident record in SorraAgents while routing the actual code change to the repo that owns the launcher. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer input required).
- **Q2 (reproduction):** How much live reproduction is acceptable? Options: (A) non-destructive evidence only (`/proc/<pid>/environ`, launcher/hook inspection, git trace2); (B) also spawn a live agent session and dump its env; (C) both. **Recommended:** C — trace2 + launcher inspection first, then one controlled fresh-session env dump to prove the end-to-end state. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer input required).
- **Q3 (regression-check placement):** The AC "a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables" — where should the check live? Options: (A) an in-repo SorraAgents test of the launch wrapper/`run_tests.py`, with the external launcher covered by its own ContextHub test; (B) in-repo only; (C) ContextHub only. **Recommended:** A — each repo tests the boundary it owns. — **OPEN QUESTION** (producer input required).

**Discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 (SorraAgents)
**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** high

## Problem statement

A parent audit can silently demote children that were already `completed` /
`in_review` (and therefore exempt from the parent's child-stage and
child-verdict blocking checks) and then fail its own closure against those
demoted stages — reporting `Ready to close: No` even when every parent
acceptance criterion is `met`. On 2026-09-27, auditing
`SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` re-screened three children whose content had changed
because the parent's commit touched files they own; each received a persisted
`Ready to close: No` child audit and was demoted (F2 →
`open`/`plan_complete`, F3 → `blocked`/`plan_complete`, F6 →
`blocked`/`plan_complete`). The parent's own verdict became `No` purely
because those children were no longer exempt, despite all six parent ACs
being `met`.

## Users and user stories

- **Audit operator** — As an audit operator, I want a parent audit to evaluate
  its own closure against the children's status as it was when the audit
  started, so an otherwise-complete parent is reported `Yes` even if a child
  is re-screened as a side effect.
- **Release manager** — As a release manager, I want a parent audit to never
  demote a completed/`in_review` child unless that child was deliberately,
  independently audited as not-ready, so a parent run cannot silently push
  completed work back into the actionable queue and cascade `blocked` states
  through the dependency chain.
- **Maintainer** — As a maintainer, I want verdicts driven only by
  unverifiable/historical or out-of-manifest ACs to be distinguishable from
  genuine code gaps, so a read-only re-audit does not downgrade an
  already-reviewed child.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Snapshot/exception semantics:** A children snapshot is taken at
   parent-audit start, and the parent's closure decision exempts every child
   that was in `in_review`/`done` (or otherwise exempt) at that point — even
   if the child's stage changed during the parent run. A parent whose own ACs
   are all `met`/`adjusted` is not blocked by children that were exempt at
   audit start.
2. **No side-effect demotion:** A child audit that is triggered as a side
   effect of a parent audit (the `--audit-children` cascade or the
   content-changed auto re-screen) does not change the child's lifecycle
   (`status`/`stage`) when the child was `in_review`/`done` before the parent
   run. Only a child explicitly and independently audited as not-ready may be
   demoted.
3. **No regression to genuine blocking:** A child that is in a pre-review
   stage (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`) or that is independently
   audited and genuinely not-ready still blocks the parent's closure. The
   existing exemption rules and the parent-first pass-through are preserved.
4. **Verdict fidelity:** ACs that are unverifiable in a read-only audit
   (historical/execution-dependent properties, or verification files outside
   the child's file-scope manifest) do not silently become blocking `partial`
   verdicts that demote an otherwise-complete item; either they are handled by
   the snapshot/no-demotion fix or they carry a distinct non-blocking
   classification.
5. **Regression test:** An automated test pins acceptance criterion 1 and 2:
   a parent audit over an `in_review` child whose only failing AC is
   unverifiable yields parent `Ready to close: Yes` and leaves the child at
   `completed`/`in_review` (or, if the chosen approach preserves the child
   stage via snapshot instead, the test asserts the parent `Yes` and the
   pre-audit child stage).
6. **Documentation:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` document the child-exemption snapshot
   / no-side-effect-demotion contract, including how `--audit-children` and
   the content-changed re-screen interact with it. All related documentation is
   updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any
   relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The audit remains **read-only** except the authorized persistence and
  verdict-driven status lifecycle; the fix must not add new state mutations.
- Must not weaken genuine blocking: a truly not-ready, independently audited
  child must still block its parent.
- Must preserve the existing `in_review`/`done` exemption, `inherited_pass`
  pass-through, and content-fingerprint freshness/reuse semantics.
- Keep the change surgical; prefer extracting shared logic over duplicating
  stage/verdict logic between `_has_phase1_blocking_issues` and
  `_build_issue_json`.
- Any change to child lifecycle must be consistent between the markdown
  report path (`_assemble_issue_report`) and the JSON path
  (`_build_issue_json`).

## Existing state

- `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()` and `_build_issue_json()` exempt children
  whose **current** `stage` is `in_review` (plus `status=completed` +
  `stage=done`, deleted, and `inherited_pass`). The exemption is evaluated at
  report-assembly time, against whatever stage the child holds *after* the
  parent run.
- The `--audit-children` cascade auto-triggers
  `audit_runner.py issue <child> --force`; that child run applies its own
  terminal lifecycle (`_apply_terminal_lifecycle`): a genuine `No` verdict
  transitions the child to `open`/`plan_complete` (and `wl` dependency state
  can surface it as `blocked`). The parent then evaluates its exemption
  against the demoted child stage and blocks.
- In the default parent-first flow, children whose content-fingerprint
  changed are re-screened and their audits persisted via
  `_persist_child_audit()`, which does not itself change the child stage — so
  the observed demotion originates in the cascade re-audit path.
- Unverifiable ACs (e.g. "the tests fail for behavioural reasons *before*
  F3–F5 land", or a file outside the child's file-scope manifest) fall to
  `partial`, a blocking verdict, which drives the child `No` and the
  subsequent demotion.

## Desired change

Make a parent audit non-destructive to already-exempt children and evaluate
the parent's closure against the child-exemption status captured at audit
start. Candidate mechanisms (the implementer may choose any that satisfies all
ACs, or a combination):

- **Snapshot exempt children at audit start** and evaluate the parent's
  closure against the snapshot rather than the post-re-audit stages
  (satisfies AC1).
- **Preserve a child's prior terminal stage** when a cascade-triggered child
  audit's verdict is driven only by unverifiable / out-of-manifest ACs
  (satisfies AC2, AC4).
- **Make child re-audit opt-in** so the default parent audit never mutates
  child lifecycle (satisfies AC2, complements AC1).
- **Introduce a distinct `unverifiable` verdict** for
  historical/execution-dependent ACs so they do not silently become blocking
  `partial` (satisfies AC4).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()`,
  `_build_issue_json()`, `_phase_children()` (cascade / auto-trigger),
  `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()`, `_child_content_changed()`,
  `_persist_child_audit()`, `_assemble_issue_report()`: snapshot exempt
  children at start; suppress side-effect demotion; keep markdown and JSON
  verdict paths consistent.
- `tests/test_audit_runner_review.py` — existing exemption/verdict unit tests
  (`test_child_audit_does_not_block_phase1_when_in_review`,
  `test_ready_false_when_child_audit_no`, etc.); add the regression test for
  AC5.
- `tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — child inclusion / lifecycle tests
  (e.g. `test_completed_in_review_child_included_in_child_results`); extend
  for the snapshot/exemption behaviour.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Status Lifecycle + child-exemption documentation.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — parent-first pass-through and
  `--audit-children` cascade documentation.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the fix needs to suppress or
  gate a lifecycle transition for cascade-triggered child audits.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Over-broad exemption (regression risk):** snapshotting "exempt at start"
  could let a genuinely broken child block-free if the parent started while
  the child was still `in_review`. Mitigation: keep the existing pre-review
  and independent-audit blocking paths intact (AC3) and add explicit tests
  for the pre-review block.
- **Fix only patches the parent decision, not the child demotion:** the child
  still ends up `open`/`blocked`, leaving the release queue inconsistent.
  Mitigation: treat AC1 and AC2 as jointly required, not alternatives.
- **Two divergent verdict paths:** `_build_issue_json()` and
  `_assemble_issue_report()` could drift. Mitigation: extract shared
  exemption/verdict logic and test both paths.
- **Cascade never re-audits genuinely changed children:** if re-audit becomes
  strictly opt-in, a changed child could inherit a stale pass. Mitigation:
  preserve the content-fingerprint gate so changed children are still
  surfaced, just not demoted by a parent-triggered run.
- **Scope creep:** other known audit defects (e.g.
  `SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`, `SA-0MUD5R5EQ000D1V2`, `SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL`) are
  related but out of scope; record them as linked work items, not scope.

## Evidence

- Parent report (all 6 ACs `met`, verdict `No`):
  `wl audit-show SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 --json`.
- Demoted children: `SA-0MUG30HV8004HV94` (now `open`/`plan_complete`),
  `SA-0MUG30IIR00978CW` and `SA-0MUG30KEV006RBAM` (now
  `blocked`/`plan_complete`), updated at `2026-09-27T01:10:42–44Z`.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63** (open) — discovered-from: the parent whose audit
  exposed the bug (all parent ACs `met`, verdict `No`).
- **SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E** (completed) — "Audit runner has circular dependency
  — child audit verdict blocks parent regardless of stage": introduced the
  `in_review` exemption this bug defeats.
- **SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0** (open) and **SA-0MUD5R5EQ000D1V2** (open) — related
  `inherited_pass` / pre-review child-stage blocking defects; coordinate to
  avoid conflicting fixes in the same exemption logic.
- **SA-0MSG9SLGI002OF7V** (completed) — precedence for "restore, never
  demote" on infrastructure-fallback verdicts; a useful pattern for the
  no-side-effect-demotion requirement.
- **SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD**, **SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P** (completed) — Phase 1 child
  AC review / child-verdict reuse and content-fingerprint freshness, which
  determine when a changed child is re-screened.

## Assumptions

- The fix is scope-limited to the `skill/audit` runner; no change to `wl`
  itself is required.
- Preserving the child's pre-audit stage (rather than snapshotting only the
  parent's decision) is the intended reading of AC3 — the implementer selects
  the concrete mechanism that satisfies both AC1 and AC2.
- `--audit-children` remains available for operators who explicitly want a
  full recursive re-audit; an explicit, independent child audit keeps its
  normal lifecycle.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed work-item description already
specified the observed behaviour, the evidence (demoted child ids, parent
report), the desired behaviour, and three candidate mitigation shapes. All
related work was resolved by worklog search and repo inspection, so no
operator/producer input was needed. This intake did not ask any questions.
